- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in subsequent 5–10 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently > true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (subtract 1–2% per day).  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “positive → negative” shifts, model overreacts to sentiment; dampen forecast sensitivity to sentiment changes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
